To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) incident and accident investigation techniques can be used to inform the design of safety-critical systems; (2) the design of safety cases can be used to identify and address safety issues; and (3) a Petri net-based formalism can be used to model safety-critical systems.

(1) incident investigations can provide a rich source of information for the design of safety-critical interactive systems, and (2) this information can be captured and formalized to support model-based design.
incident investigations can inform the design and development of interactive safety-critical systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing an approach for using incident and accident investigation techniques to inform the development and validation of formal models of safety-critical systems.
the development of a systematic approach to the use of incident investigation data to support the development of safety cases and formal system models.
the use of information from past incidents and accidents to inform the design of safety-critical interactive systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the approach presented in this paper is useful to inform model-based design of safety-critical interactive systems, and that it is a useful complement to the more established approaches of using scenarios, usability analysis and the use of metrics.
the approach is a promising one that can be applied to the design of safety-critical interactive systems.
the incident investigation data and knowledge can be used to support the design of safety cases for interactive systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the approach can help to identify and prevent potential safety-critical issues that could be overlooked by traditional methods.
we are able to use the information from an accident investigation to inform a model-based safety analysis of a system.
we have demonstrated that the information from incident investigation reports can be used to inform model-based design of safety-critical interactive systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proposed approach can help designers and safety analysts to develop a more comprehensive understanding of the system and to identify potential risks and hazards that may have been missed in traditional design processes.

incident investigation reports can be a rich source of data and knowledge to inform the development and validation of safety-cases for interactive safety-critical systems, as well as the development and validation formal models of such systems.
incident investigations can be used to inform formal models that can, in their turn, be used in a model-based design of safety-critical interactive systems.
